sentences.text: Palaeobates was a small shark that grew to a length of about 1 meter.
Scientists have found thirty-three recorded fossil occurrences of this genus.
Its unique teeth were built for crushing hard shells rather than tearing flesh.
The genus was first described by Meyer in 1849.
Analysis of dental microwear suggests the animal ate bivalves, gastropods, crustaceans, and echinoderms.
The teeth exhibit orthodont histology, a specific internal structure.
Palaeobates is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
It belongs to the family Acrodontidae.
The type species for the genus is the extinct Psammodus angustissimus.
Three species are known: Palaeobates polaris, Palaeobates reticulatus, and Palaeobates verzilini.
Palaeobates lived during the Triassic period.
